timeline.event: Ardashir I founds the Sasanian Empire
The last Sasanian king, Yazdegerd III, dies fleeing the Arab conquest
Ferdowsi completes the Shahnameh, the Persian Book of Kings
Hulagu Khan's Mongols take the fortress of Alamut
Shah Ismail I founds the Safavid dynasty
Shah Abbas I makes Isfahan his capital
Nader Shah sacks Delhi and seizes the Peacock Throne
The Qajars make Tehran the capital
Iran's first parliament opens during the Constitutional Revolution
Reza Shah founds the Pahlavi dynasty
Persia asks the world to call it Iran
Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin meet at the Tehran Conference
Prime Minister Mosaddegh nationalises Iran's oil industry
A referendum establishes the Islamic Republic of Iran
Maryam Mirzakhani becomes the first woman to win the Fields Medal

places.name: Tehran
places.clue: Iran's capital since 1786 sprawls beneath the Alborz mountains and is home to the Golestan Palace and Azadi Tower.

places.name: Isfahan
places.clue: Shah Abbas I's Safavid capital, famed for Naqsh-e Jahan Square and the saying 'Isfahan is half the world'.

places.name: Persepolis
places.clue: Ceremonial capital of the Achaemenid kings, begun by Darius I and burned by Alexander the Great in 330 BCE.

places.name: Mount Damavand
places.clue: At about 5,610 m, this dormant volcano is Iran's highest peak and the tallest volcano in Asia.

places.name: Mashhad
places.clue: Iran's second-largest city is home to the shrine of Imam Reza, the country's most visited pilgrimage site.

places.name: Yazd
places.clue: A desert city of mud-brick lanes, windcatchers and Zoroastrian fire temples, UNESCO-listed in 2017.

places.name: Tabriz
places.clue: The first Safavid capital, whose vast covered bazaar is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

places.name: Susa
places.clue: Capital of ancient Elam and later a royal city of Darius I, where Hammurabi's law code was found in 1901.

places.name: Lut Desert
places.clue: Wind-carved ridges called kaluts rise from one of the hottest places on Earth, UNESCO-listed in 2016.

places.name: Behistun Inscription
places.clue: Darius I's trilingual cliff inscription here helped scholars decipher cuneiform in the 19th century.

places.name: Shahr-e Sukhteh
places.clue: This 'Burnt City' was a Bronze Age trading hub in Sistan and is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

places.name: Gonbad-e Qabus
places.clue: An early 11th-century tomb tower, celebrated as the tallest tower ever built purely of brick.
